To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
OPN alters the functional profile and the activation of porcine brain macroglia in vitro.
OPN alters the functional profile and the activation of microglia in a dose‐dependent manner.
the glycoprotein osteopontin (OPN) is able to shift the functional profile of microglia towards a neuroprotective phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of OPN in microglia and the potential of this cytokine as a therapeutic agent.
the role of osteopontin in modulating the functional profile of microglia in the CNS.
the role of OPN as an immunomodulator of microglial function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OPN is a cytokine which can be secreted by microglia and can alter microglial function in vitro.
OPN is an important regulator of microglial function in vitro.
OPN shifts the phenotype of microglia towards the immune‐balanced profile of microglia in the healthy CNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OPN, in addition to its role in bone remodelling, is a multifunctional molecule with a role in the CNS.
OPN is a microglia‐modulating cytokine, and its expression in the CNS may contribute to the maintenance of a homeostatic microenvironment.
OPN is a microglia modulator that can be produced by cells of the CNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OPN is an important modulator of microglial function.
OPN, a cytokine that is up‐regulated by glial and immune cells, may have a dual effect on microglial functions, depending on the context.
the OPN‐microglia interaction is not limited to a single functional outcome.
